title: Infrastructure
no_org: Choose an organization to see where its products run.
no_backend: This Studio has no environments yet (the backend predates them).
about: Where {org}'s products run: the places it holds (a cluster, a Constructor Research project, the registry images come from), the environments it defines on them, dev to prod, and what runs where.
about_deploys: A deploy runs on the server with the environment's connection: nobody's laptop holds the cluster's credentials. An environment is added from the place it runs on; a release climbs the ladder, each environment taking from the one before it.
add_place_cluster: a Kubernetes cluster, by its kubeconfig
add_place_research: your sign-in to a Research project
add_place_research_kit: comes with the Constructor Research kit: install it under Kits
add_place_registry: where images and charts are pushed
no_environment: No environment yet · add dev, stage or prod from a place
protected_title: Protected: a deploy waits for an administrator's approval
strictness_dev_title: Products are checked as development ones here: the production rules only warn
strictness_prod_title: Products are checked as production ones here
place_unseen: a place this page cannot see
remove_body: What runs in the cluster stays there.
no_place: No place yet · connect a cluster, a Research project or a registry
unseen_cluster: A cluster this page cannot see
out_of_reach: its connection is out of reach
research_own_signin: each member signs in with their own account
open_to_projects_title: A project may add environments of its own on it, without an administrator (ADR-0054 §2)
research_each_member: Each member builds and deploys with their own sign-in (ADR-0049 §5).
projects_may_add: may add environments of their own here
projects_use_org: use only the organization's environments here
nothing_runs_here: Nothing runs here · deploy from a project's Releases
preview_title: A preview: its own namespace beside the environment, removed when it expires
no_pods: No pods of this release run in {namespace}.
nothing_runs: Nothing runs anywhere yet · deploy from a project's Releases
runs_on_research: The Constructor Research project it runs in is chosen below; every member builds and deploys there with their own sign-in.
runs_on_added_from: The cluster this was added from. Add an environment on another cluster from that cluster's panel.
runs_on_kubernetes: A Kubernetes cluster of the organization
runs_on_research_option: Constructor Research: its hardware, its registry, its addresses
field_registry_placeholder: ghcr.io/acme — where the product's images are pulled from
registry_login_hint: The cluster pulls the product's images with it, and a published chart is fetched with it.
pull_login_hint: A read-only login for the cluster to pull with. Without one, the cluster gets the login builds push with, which can write to the registry.
field_builder_image_placeholder: ghcr.io/acme/mirror/builder@sha256:… — empty: the one Studio ships with
builder_image_hint: From the organization's own mirror, named by digest, so every build runs the same builder.
builder_login_none: None — the builder image is public
build_namespace_hint: A pattern like the namespace pattern: where a project's build Job runs, apart from what it deploys.
field_namespaces_placeholder: web-dev, web-build — empty: Studio creates its own
namespaces_hint: When Studio may not create namespaces on this cluster, the ones its administrators made for Studio to use.
broad_token: A build's registry token may reach past the project's own path (only for a registry that cannot scope one)
infra_where: Where a product's PostgreSQL, Keycloak and the like run
infra_with_product: With the product, one of each per environment
infra_shared_not_dev: The organization's shared place (not in a dev environment)
infra_dev_hint: A dev environment always runs them with the product, so a product never signs in through Studio's own identity provider.
infra_shared_hint: One service per line: its name, where it runs (@namespace), and what it provides. Passwords go in the project's configuration secrets.
infra_ingress: Public address of a service (its Ingress)
infra_ingress_hint: A service the project gives a public address gets an Ingress at that host and path, so the address answers. One annotation per line, key=value.
namespace_pattern_hint: A pattern, not a name: {project} becomes each project's name and {environment} this environment's.
database_own_research: The product's own, when its gears keep data: a Postgres service in its Research application
database_own_cluster: The product's own, when its gears keep data: a Postgres in its namespace, with every deploy
database_shared: A shared Postgres — recorded only: deploys get no database from it
promote_anywhere: Anywhere: any build may be deployed here
previews: Previews: a project may try a build here in a namespace of its own, removed when it expires
preview_domain_placeholder: preview.example.com — a wildcard DNS record to the cluster's ingress; empty: no address
strictness_default_prod: production, as a protected environment does
strictness_default_dev: development, as an unprotected environment does
strictness_dev: development: the production rules only warn
strictness_prod: production: a production rule that fails stops the build
strictness_hint: What the engine checks the product against when it is built for here (ADR-0060). A development check lets a product without an identity provider or a tenant resolver build, and says what it lacks.
protected: Protected: a deploy waits for an organization administrator's approval
every_project: Every project of the organization may deploy here
research_connection_hint: Your own sign-in to Research (Connections), to pick the project. Every member builds and deploys with their own sign-in; the project's owner adds them to it in Research.
research_project_hint: Each Studio project runs there as one application per environment, named
research_unreachable: Research could not list the projects ({error}); type the id.
research_trial: trial: Research ends what runs on it by its own rules
connect_cluster_hint: A kubeconfig with the cluster's CA and a service-account token, or a bare token for a cluster whose certificate a public CA signed. Stored in credstore for the organization; only the server uses it, to deploy.
bootstrap_title: Prepare the cluster once, as its administrator
bootstrap_hint: Every project gets its own namespace, {namespace}, made by the first deploy into it. This manifest lets the {account} account make those namespaces and give itself {role} in them, and nothing else. Apply it with {command}, then paste the token the comment at its top shows how to read. Kubernetes 1.30 or newer.
kubeconfig_or_paste: or paste a token or a kubeconfig below
connect_registry_hint: Where the product's images and chart are published: ghcr.io, a Harbor project, a GitLab registry. A robot account or a token that can read it is enough for deploys. Stored in credstore for the organization; only the server uses it.
registry_username_placeholder: robot$acme+deployer — empty for a token alone
registry_token_placeholder: the robot's secret or a read token
assignments_hint: Which namespace each project deploys into in each environment, and where its builds run. Needed where the cluster gives Studio namespaces instead of letting it create them; a namespace a run made is recorded here too.
no_assignments: No namespace assigned yet · Studio creates its own where the cluster lets it
retention_unreadable: The retention could not be read
retention_org_hint: Every project that has none of its own follows this. A project sets its own in Releases › Images.
keep_days: Keep what is younger than, days
retention_always: What runs somewhere and what is pinned is kept whatever these say.
registry_empty_body: A build in Studio pushes the product's images and chart here.
not_recorded_title: No record of Studio names it
delete_version_title: Delete this version from the registry
delete_version_body: It is deleted from the registry, every tag of it with it. A deploy that names it cannot pull it again.
no_digest_to_delete: The registry's listing gives no digest for it.
